source.title: ANCHOR: An External LLM-Driven Supervisory Module Facilitating Healthy Evolution in Self-Evolving Systems
source.authors: Dian-Xing Shi; Bo-Wen Wang; Jun He; Junhao Chen; Yuta Nakashima

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some tables have flattened/OCR artifacts, and the supplementary safety values for R-Zero differ from the main table.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates safety outcomes after benign-task self-evolution, a different training setting from ordinary fine-tuning on benign instruction examples.
record.gate_note: The paper's cited claims about benign fine-tuning are background only and are not counted as results. Rows record the paper's own harmful-prompt ASR results for base backbones and self-evolved variants. The reward-hacking benchmark measures a related but distinct behavior and is not included as evidence for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-prompt ASR (HarmBench, HEx-PHI, SaladBench) before and after self-evolving RL on benign, self-generated coding and math tasks. For the AZR series, started from safety-tuned Qwen2.5 Instruct models, this bears on V2 in a new training setting. R-Zero starts from Qwen3 Base models, which are not safety-trained, so it does not bear on V2. ANCHOR and [+SP] add safety supervision or safety prompts, so they are mitigation conditions rather than plain benign training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right: ANCHOR mitigates safety degradation in self-evolution while largely keeping coding and math ability; execution-result feedback matters most; supervision frequency shows diminishing returns. Add that the authors describe plain AZR/R-Zero as showing safety degradation (mis-evolution). Their own ASR Avg numbers show this only for some AZR models; R-Zero and AZR-7B ASR falls.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates phase-conditioned LLM supervision during self-evolving agent training, not the original fine-tuning intervention or token-position KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model family and scale; the detailed supplementary ASR table and main Table 1 give different R-Zero values.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-evolution on non-safety-trained Qwen3 Base models lowers ASR Avg (20.1→16.0 at 4B; 19.2→12.8 at 8B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign self-play RL on base, unaligned models changes harmful compliance.

fits_no_version.finding: Memory-induced reward-hacking resistance (RR) falls after self-evolution in most models, e.g. AZR-7B 56.1→36.6 and R-Zero-8B 61.0→34.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-evolution increases reward-hacking or misevolution behaviour toward deployment policies.

fits_no_version.finding: ANCHOR and static safety prompts during self-evolution lower ASR relative to plain AZR/R-Zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time LLM supervision mitigates safety drift in self-evolving agents.

record.problems: The reported evaluation averages three runs but gives no uncertainty estimates. ASR values for R-Zero variants differ between the main table and Supplementary Material C.1. The benign-data setting is self-evolution on generated tasks, not conventional benign instruction fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant ASR rows were left out. Coding, math, and reward-hacking metrics were not extracted as rows because they do not measure the harmful-prompt compliance named by the tested version.

untested.parts: Conventional SFT on ordinary or selected benign instruction data. Only self-play RL on self-generated code/math tasks is tested.
All: no per-token KL or position analysis.
All: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
All: no analysis of why safety is shallow.
All: ANCHOR is prompt-level supervision, not training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The record's column mapping in Supp. Table 1 is wrong. The 'ASR Avg' values are HarmBench, as (HB+HEX+SB)/3 reproduces the main-table ASR Avg. With the correct mapping there is no R-Zero main/supplement discrepancy. ASR reported as averages of 3 runs with no uncertainty. Qi et al. 2023 is cited only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal after a few to a few hundred harmful examples.
Conventional fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data. The tested setting is benign-task self-evolution.
Per-token KL divergence by response position.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Localization of safety behavior in weights, parameters, or ranks.
Whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
Training intended to deepen safety and its robustness.
